transit.description: Internal no-op graph edge (transit-node pattern). Propagates source changes through declared workspace dependencies without serializing check-types tasks. App-to-app service bindings are not package dependencies and require an explicit callee#transit edge in the caller's package configuration.

check-types.description: Type-check with tsc --noEmit. Uses the transit node (not ^check-types) so packages run in parallel while still invalidating when dependency source changes. JIT packages export source .ts directly, so no declaration emit or project references. No `types` edge: worker-configuration.d.ts is committed, so it is a tracked $TURBO_DEFAULT$ input and hashes directly - regenerating it here would dirty the tree mid-CI.

types.description: Regenerate the committed worker-configuration.d.ts (wrangler types). Writes a tracked source file, so it is uncached like the other write-mode tasks - run it after editing wrangler.jsonc, then commit the result. CI verifies freshness with types:check instead of running this.

types:check.description: Verify the committed worker-configuration.d.ts still matches wrangler.jsonc (wrangler types --check). Read-only and cached; fails when the file has drifted, prompting `pnpm types` + commit. Unlike `types`, --check does not start workerd, so it is cheap in CI.

build.description: Build production output to dist/; gated on the package's own check-types and upstream builds.

dev.description: Run the local dev server (persistent, uncached).

preview.description: Serve the production build locally (persistent, uncached).

deploy.description: Bootstrap / emergency path: wrangler deploy (upload + immediate 100%). Not the recurring Stage 1 main path — use upload then human promote.

upload.description: Stage 1: wrangler versions upload for the production env. Creates an immutable version without changing the active deployment. Human promote is a separate path.

promote.description: Human-only Stage 1 promote: wrangler versions deploy (interactive). Must not be invoked from CI; the upload credential is deployment-capable.
